sources.name: Financial Intelligence Centre Guidance Note 3A - client identification and verification

entries.subject: official_identity_document_definition
entries.display: An official identity document is the green bar-coded ID document; old ID books do not qualify
entries.quote: The Department of Home Affairs describes an official identity document as a green bar -coded identity document.
entries.notes: Guidance Note 3A issued July 2005 under s4(c) of the FIC Act.

entries.subject: old_identity_documents_not_acceptable
entries.display: Old (pre-green-barcode) identity documents may not be treated as official identity documents
entries.quote: Therefore, old identity documents may not be construed as official identity documents.

entries.subject: alternative_identity_documents
entries.display: Driver's licence or SA passport may be accepted where no official ID can be produced
entries.quote: The following are examples of documents that may be accepted in such exceptional circumstances as an alternative form of verification: South African driver's licence; or South African passport.
entries.notes: Allowed set: South African driver's licence; South African passport. Requires a recorded reason and a document showing photograph, names, date of birth and identity number.

entries.subject: foreign_national_identity_document
entries.display: For foreign nationals the identification document is the passport of their country of citizenship
entries.quote: The Regulations furthermore define an identification document in respect of a natural person who is not a citizen of the Republic and not resident in the Republic as a passport issued by the country of which that person is a citizen.

entries.subject: proof_of_address_currency
entries.display: Proof of residential address should be less than three months old
entries.quote: Since the documentation must be current, a good practice would be to require documentation that is less than three months old.
entries.notes: Stated as good practice rather than a hard rule.

entries.subject: dha_address_slip_not_proof_of_address
entries.display: Department of Home Affairs address slips do not verify residential address
entries.quote: It is the view of the Centre that the address slips issued by the Department of Home Affairs do not constitute information that can reasonably be expected to achieve verification of a person's current address.

entries.subject: acceptable_proof_of_address_utility_bill
entries.display: A utility bill in the client's name and showing the residential address is acceptable proof of address
entries.quote: a utility bill reflecting the name and residential address of the person
entries.notes: Non-exhaustive list also includes bank statement, lease, municipal rates invoice, mortgage statement, telephone account, TV licence, insurance policy, vehicle licence and retail statement.

entries.subject: proof_of_tax_number_required
entries.display: A SARS-issued proof of income tax number is required; an IRP5 is not accepted
entries.quote: Proof of income tax number, for example, a copy of an official document issued by the South African Revenue Services (SARS). An IRP5 will not be accepted.
entries.notes: Standard Bank SBG Securities onboarding list for South African individuals; page undated, captured 2026-11-02.

entries.subject: certified_id_copy_requirement
entries.display: Onboarding requires an original certified copy of a valid SA ID or an unexpired passport for foreign nationals
entries.quote: Original certified copy of a valid South Africa Identification Document or a valid unexpired passport in the case of a foreign national.
entries.notes: Standard Bank SBG Securities onboarding list; page undated.

entries.subject: popia_regulator_establishment
entries.display: The Information Regulator is established by section 39 of POPIA (Act 4 of 2013)
entries.quote: The Information Regulator (South Africa) is an independent body established in terms of section 39 of the Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013.
entries.notes: POPIA is Act 4 of 2013; the page is the Regulator's own site.

entries.subject: information_officer_registration
entries.display: Information Officers may only assume duties after registration with the Regulator (POPIA s55)
entries.quote: In accordance with the stipulations laid out in Section 55 of the Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA), Information Officers must assume their duties only after the responsible party has registered them with the Regulator.

notes: FICA customer due diligence comes from FIC Guidance Note 3A (primary) and Standard Bank's onboarding list. POPIA obligations are taken from the Information Regulator's own site. No source in this corpus states a monetary CDD threshold, so none is asserted.
